investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 slots available), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 kata nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256 to fail completely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 slots available), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 kata nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256 to fail completely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-02 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler could not place the pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 kata-peerpods-capable nodes had no remaining VM slots, and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector constraints. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~143–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing empty evidence and a complete contract gap for all required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
